uncertainties: The same 1910 source gives conflicting exterior dimensions; measurement datums remain unresolved.

Waiting-room dimensions refer to several different datums: external lantern 325×119 ft, structural frame 320×112 ft 10 in, reported room 314 ft 4 in×108 ft 8 in, clear room 277×103 ft. Exact finished-wall control points remain to be reconciled.
Full circa-1935–1940 alterations, signage, furnishing locations and surrounding parcels remain unverified.
Materials and lighting are reconstruction choices, not calibrated measurements from monochrome photographs.
Incomplete ornament and contextual masses must not be described as authenticated historic details.
Reference photographs support comparison; matching cameras and a full architectural review remain required.

architecturalDimensions.method: Read from original plate image; floor datum is the waiting-room floor, not the street.

roofLunette.page: Printed p. 12; original page image visually checked
roofLunette.glazingEvidence: Plate 302 depicts five tall primary glazing divisions within each lunette. Three refers to the windows on each long wall, not subdivisions within one window.
roofLunette.labelledDatumSource: S2 plate 302, elevation line through thermal-window sill region and centres of circular features at the window bases; their identity as operational clocks is not established by this section alone
roofLunette.labelledDatumScope: Both section margins read ELEVATION 421.25, corroborated by the drawn distance 65 ft 9 in below roof E487. Exact offsets to clear glazing bottom and sill mouldings remain to be resolved; the 31 m glazing-base height is a close inference.

levelEvidence.streetDatumScope: Plate 302 at 33rd Street shows ELEVATION334.000. A single flat globalstreet is a working simplification; Seventh/Eighth curb gradients have not been surveyed.
levelEvidence.waitingFloorReading: 1926 drawing leftlabel 320 ft 0¾in; newpassage finishedfloor 319 ft 11 in level; adjacent waitingfloor varies slightly. Rightlabel fraction not certified from available raster.
levelEvidence.status: Cross-source supported working elevation; exact sidewalk and floor gradients remain uncertain.
levelEvidence.circulation: Arcade is at streetlevel. Grandstair descends to waitingroom. Waitingroom, subsidiarywaitingrooms and main departureconcourse share the lower mainlevel. Exitconcourse is belowmain and aboveplatforms.
levelEvidence.warning: PRR promotional 18 ft exitheight, Gibbs 17 ft exitlift and 27 ft 6 in mainlift, and Francis 27 ft waitingaboveTOPRAIL refer to differing destinations/datums and cannot be combined indiscriminately.
levelEvidence.platformEvidence: Gibbs ASCE LXIX printed p 261 explicitly specifies New York station platforms; plateLXXVIII independently dimensions 3 ft 10 in.
levelEvidence.independentRoofConsistency: MainE320 +167 ft highestroof =E487; streetE334 +153 ft highestroof =E487. This independently supports 14 ft main-to-street working registration.

clockEvidence.exterior: Four exterior clocks, each 6 ft diameter
clockEvidence.publicRooms: Fourteen instruments, 18 in to 15 ft diameter
clockEvidence.mainWaitingRoom: One motor-driven 15 ft dial explicitly described

clockEvidence.scope: Section 302 alone does not establish six operational 15 ft clocks at its circular window-base features; locations and 1935 changes require photograph matching
